output.summary: The yield decline is real: the CMM gauge R&R is stable, and Halvard's receiving PPM rose. The new-operator hypothesis is contradicted, because new and experienced operators reject at similar rates and FPY fell before new operators ran alone. Fatigue, Corvane hardness spread and spindle wear are all confounded. The steel change, the deferred spindle service and the 12-hour shifts all arrived within weeks of each other, and the scrap tag times do not show when parts were cut. A split trial can separate them: serve the spindles in two groups, run Tamsworth lots alongside Corvane, and recover the machining hour from the cycle counters. The Line 6 Corvane results are a cheap extra check. Reverting shifts or blaming steel now is premature. Disciplining new operators or sampling inspection would be harmful.
